text.en: A bicycle wheel touches the road at just one point. That line touching a circle at one point is called a tangent.

A tangent to a circle is a line that meets the circle at exactly one point, called the point of contact.
A secant is a line that cuts the circle at two points.
Theorem one: the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
So a tangent makes a right angle with the radius at the point where it touches.
At any point on a circle there is one and only one tangent.
The perpendicular to a tangent at its point of contact passes through the centre of the circle.
Example: radius OP = 5 and OQ = 13 where PQ is a tangent at P. Then PQ = root(169 - 25) = 12.
The proof is by contradiction: if OP were not perpendicular, a closer point on the tangent would lie inside the circle.

problem.en: A tangent PQ at point P of a circle with centre O meets OQ at Q. If OP = 3 cm and OQ = 5 cm, find PQ.

text.en: OP is perpendicular to PQ, so triangle OPQ is right angled at P.

why.en: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius.

prompt.en: What is special about a tangent and the radius?

points.en: A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point.
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
Use Pythagoras with the radius, tangent and line from the centre.
